speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are concerned about the increasing yellow discoloration in your newborn's eyes and skin. To understand the cause, how many days old is the baby, and when did you first notice the jaundice?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (Physiologic Jaundice).

The baby's age (2 weeks), weight gain (normal), and exclusive breastfeeding history strongly support this benign diagnosis over pathological causes like sepsis or hemolysis, which typically present earlier. I will now monitor for any signs of dehydration or failure to thrive to ensure she remains well-hydrated.
